chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ali al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you stand in the last two rak'ahs, do not recite in them, but say: Al-hamdu lillahi, Subhanallah, wa Allahu Akbar." He was only prohibited from reciting with the conviction that nothing else would suffice, not that he should not recite it as a choice or to seek merit, and this is not contradictory to what we mentioned. As for what the Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned regarding the final Tashahhud, we have already presented the first Tashahhud, and now we will mention the second Tashahhud, then we will clarify the minimum that is permissible to restrict oneself to in the Tashahhud, if Allah wills.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: Tashahhud (the testimonies of faith in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should be recited in the last two rak'ahs of prayer instead of Surahs?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal nuance of recitation in the final two rak'ahs, distinguishing between obligatory sufficiency and optional merit. It serves as a foundational text for the Shia jurisprudence of Salat, emphasizing that limiting oneself to specific dhikr does not invalidate the prayer, thereby addressing potential misconceptions among worshippers. The commentary further bridges this ruling to the structural requirements of the Tashahhud, highlighting the meticulous attention to detail in Shia ritual practice.
